inputs.text: ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.

fields.description: Fog warning: thick fog is expected in western regions of the UAE. Visibility may drop to zero at times from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Drive with extreme caution. More: https://alerts.example.ae
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions tonight until 10:00 Wednesday
fields.instruction: If you drive, slow down, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow the modified speed limits. Follow all traffic safety guidelines.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was excluded on that basis.
No specific roads, towns or emirates are named, because the NCM statement only says 'several western regions of the UAE'.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and certainty to Likely because NCM describes 'potential' fog, but says visibility may fall to zero. Please confirm whether you want Severe instead. Also check that the operator's 'Western region (demo zone)' matches NCM's 'several western regions'.

objections.fix: Reword to follow the bulletin, e.g. 'Fog may form in several western regions of the UAE, and visibility is expected to drop, possibly to zero at times, from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Take extra care where fog is thick.'
objections.issue: The description overstates the bulletin. The bulletin warns of 'potential fog formation' and mentions thick fog only 'in areas experiencing thick fog'. The alert instead says thick fog is expected across the western regions, which makes certainty and extent higher than NCM stated.

payload.summary: The hazard, times (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb), area (western regions) and zero-visibility wording match the verified NCM bulletin, and the alert contains no unverified reports. One problem: the description says thick fog is expected everywhere in the area. The bulletin only warns of potential fog formation and mentions thick fog only for some areas, so the alert overstates certainty and extent.

no_basis.concern: The sender is a demo stand-in for the real issuer, but it is sending an 'Actual' public alert from a live console. UAE-PORTAL-EWS#0027 limits sending to named entities (NCEMA, MoI, police, MoHAP). Approvers should confirm that the stand-in sender is intended for live, real-event use.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause or recorded gap stating whether a demo or stand-in issuer registered for all areas and categories may send Actual alerts in a live environment.

payload.summary: The sender is in the issuer register at level 1, with all areas and all categories. The alert area (Western region demo zone, DEMO-ZONE/AUH-WEST) matches the area drawn for event uae-fog-2026-02-17. Status 'Actual' fits the real-event context and the live console. As a new 'Alert' with no references, it needs none. No active alerts from other authorities could be overreached. Nothing within my mandate is wrong.

no_basis.concern: The action, 'Drive with extreme caution' / 'قُد بحذر شديد', is not on the first page in either language. The English first page (about 93 characters) ends partway through the visibility sentence. The Arabic first page (41 characters) holds only the hazard heading and part of the first sentence. A reader who sees only page 1 gets the hazard but not the action. The drafter could move a short action phrase up, e.g. 'Fog warning: drive with extreme caution...'.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring the first cell broadcast page to carry the hazard and the protective action (search 'alert first page hazard action'). The returned TDRA TS FS 001, 3GPP TS 23.041 and WMO CAP clauses cover language, display and page structure, but none sets first-page content.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. English is 218 characters in GSM-7, which comes to 3 pages; Arabic is 228 characters in UCS-2, which comes to 6 pages. Both are under the 15-page cell broadcast maximum. Each language's encoding suits its script, and the page counts match 93 GSM-7 or 41 UCS-2 characters per 82-octet page. Length is already covered by G6. One concern has no supporting clause: the action is not on the first page in either language. I have listed it under no_basis.

payload.summary: The Arabic headline, description and instruction match the English in meaning. Times (21:30 tonight, 10:00 Wednesday), dates (Tue 17 Feb, Wed 18 Feb), place (western regions of the UAE), hazard (thick fog, visibility may drop to zero at times) and URL are all carried over correctly. The protective actions are complete and correct: slow down, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, follow the modified speed limits, follow all traffic safety guidelines, and drive with extreme caution. I found no difference in meaning. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named person who reads Arabic must still approve it before sending.

fields.description: Fog may form in several western regions of the UAE. Visibility is expected to drop, possibly to zero at times, from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Take extra care where fog is thick.
fields.headline: Fog may reduce visibility in western regions tonight until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb
fields.instruction: Drive with extreme caution, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow all traffic safety guidelines. Strictly obey modified speed limits, especially where fog is thick.
left_out: No inputs were unverified, so none were excluded for that reason.
The issuer site (https://alerts.example.ae) was left out of the short phone text to keep it focused on the hazard. It can be added if a link is wanted.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I followed the Met reviewer's wording and set certainty to Possible because NCM says 'potential fog'. Change it to Likely if you read 'visibility is expected to deteriorate' as the main message. NCM names only 'several western regions', so please confirm that the operator's 'Western region (demo zone)' matches that area.

payload.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin. It covers the same hazard (fog and low visibility, possibly zero at times), the same window (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb) and the same area wording (several western regions). Its advice also follows the bulletin. Certainty 'Possible' fits the bulletin's 'potential fog formation' wording, and the alert contains no unverified material.

no_basis.concern: The registered sender is a demo authority standing in for the real issuer, yet the context is a real event on a live console. Under the national system, only entities such as NCEMA, the Ministry of Interior, police or the Ministry of Health may send warnings. A person should confirm that the demo issuer is meant to act for the real authority here. No clause addresses stand-in issuers, so this is not an objection.
no_basis.searched_for: Clauses on delegated or stand-in issuers, or on using a demo or test sender identity for Actual alerts.

no_basis.concern: The first page does not carry the action in either language. English page 1 (about 93 GSM-7 characters) ends around 'Visibility is expected to drop, possibly'. Arabic page 1 (41 UCS-2 characters) covers only 'قد يتكوّن الضباب في عدة مناطق غربية من دول…'. The action 'Take extra care where fog is thick' / 'توخّوا مزيدًا من الحذر…' appears only on the last page (page 3 in English, page 6 in Arabic). A recipient who reads only the first page sees the hazard but no instruction. Suggested fix if a basis is found: move the action sentence near the start of both texts.
